extracted.intended_audience: communications professionals, PR/media-relations people, and video producers pitching or supplying footage to broadcast newsrooms
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for creating, selecting, and packaging B-roll (supporting video footage) so it is useful, broadcast‑ready, and attractive to TV news producers and editors. Focuses on relevance, technical quality, shot variety/duration, archive use, and matching outlet style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the story
rubrics_metrics.description: You need relevant, engaging video content to support a TV news story; without a strong visual aid, TV broadcasters may overlook your story altogether.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide footage that directly illustrates or relates to the narrative or interviewee's points. Irrelevant or tangential shots reduce the likelihood a producer will select the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and visual interest
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll helps to address challenges by providing both context and visual interest to a story by supporting the main footage; it might be deployed to demonstrate what the interviewee is describing or to avoid uninteresting footage of just one person talking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use B-roll to show actions, locations, products, or processes referenced in the piece so viewers understand and remain engaged. Avoid static, uninformative shots that don't add meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/broadcast quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the footage is important — producers will reject footage that lacks quality or requires extensive editing; TV is less tolerant of rough edits (e.g., jump cuts) than many online outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shoot to broadcast standards where possible (stable framing, good exposure, clean audio on cutaways, steady camera movement). Poorly shot or noisy footage is less likely to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability for editing (covering mistakes and cuts)
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll can be used to cover up mistakes and other cuts in the footage and to avoid uninteresting single‑talking‑head footage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide footage that allows editors to hide jump cuts, patch together interviews, or replace filler shots. Anti-patterns: forcing editors to use white flashes, punch in/out shots, or extensive jump cuts because no B-roll exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shot variety and General Views (GVs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule of thumb: provide around 5-10 mins of General Views (GVs), including a variety of both static wide and close shots, with some accompanying slow movement shots like pans and tilts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple focal lengths (wide, medium, close) and both static and slowly moving shots so editors have options. The quoted 5–10 minutes guideline helps maintain a consistent flow of visuals for different story needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shot length and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the shots longer and more varied — length and timings of shots are often crucial to filling a gap seamlessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor longer takes and mix durations so editors can cut to the pace they need; include slow pans/tilts and sustained wide or close frames rather than many quick, short clips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an archive/bank of B-roll
rubrics_metrics.description: When capturing new footage becomes a logistical hurdle, having a bank of B-roll and archive video allows a newsroom to maintain a consistent flow of compelling visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and tag an archive for fast retrieval during unforeseen events or for stories in hard-to-reach locations. Example uses cited: vaccination program coverage, lockdown impacts, major events with limited access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness in extraordinary or hard-to-reach situations
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll’s value becomes even more apparent in extraordinary situations, and for stories in hard-to-reach locations — it can allow stations to provide comprehensive coverage without compromising visual quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize capturing broadly usable visuals (establishing shots, relevant activity, contextual scenes) that can be repurposed across multiple stories when access is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match outlet style and editorial preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent and style of B-roll deployment varies between news outlets (e.g., BBC tends to keep shots simple, clear and slow, while Channel 4 news is more dynamic and stylistic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor B-roll to the target broadcaster’s aesthetic and pacing. Research the outlet’s style and supply footage that fits their visual language rather than a one-size-fits-all package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness, originality and resource awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Original footage is valuable but harder to obtain under tight deadlines and stretched newsroom resources; mobile phones and social media help source video but time pressure makes original footage difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible provide original, timely footage; when not possible, supply high-quality archive material. Be mindful that quality footage takes time and money — positioning B-roll as time/money-saving for a newsroom increases its appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic/value proposition to newsrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing B-roll offers newsrooms value — saving them time and money, while giving them options that can create more interesting edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight how supplied B-roll reduces newsroom workload (less need for remote shoots or expensive pickups) and increases the chances of getting airtime. Frame B-roll as a practical asset, not an optional extra.
